1. I've had some recent success (with lots of manual intervention) getting Agents to rewrite a code base from LangFoo into Rust.

  2. For those who have attempted to use agents to rewrite Lean4 into Rust -- any partial success ? (Even of a small part of the full system?)
But why would you want to do that?

Analogous rewrites show ~30x speedups at the parser/frontend level. A fast Rust kernel could act as a prima facie assessor — quickly triaging whether candidate proofs are well-formed before full Lean elaboration. Useful for batch verification in large formalization projects. I might try this myself! @TongKe Xue you might have set me on a wild diversion :working_on_it:

As far as I can see, Lean 4 was specifically designed so that the compiler could be written in Lean 4.
The speedup potential is real, but it beats the self-hosting purpose...

let's see which stage it gets stuck on :-)

Apparently the C++ code is very well structured, making it easy for Claude (1) write the Rust layer by layer and (2) diff vs C++ layer one layer at a time.
I have something that claims it can verify olean files. Besides cloning math4lib, is there an 'olean torture test'? (I want to test C++ vs vibe-coded Rust).

I don't know if the olean verifier is actually correct (i.e. something that accepts everything would also pass this test), as I haven't found the 'olean torture tests' of negative examples. Going to see if Rust version can also match mmap speed + start actually interpreting lean.

https://github.com/tkxue/unofficial_lean4_rs/

I'm 99.9999999% sure this is broken.

This was generated by cloning the lean4 repls, and repeatedly asking claude

"What else do we need to get Rust to run Mathlib lean4 files?"

The core problem is -- I have no evidence this rejects incorrect 'proofs'.

There is something that sorta looks like a REPL. Maybe there is something interesting here.

If you want a first test of it you can tell your agent friend to vibe code your vibe coded checker into https://github.com/leanprover/lean-kernel-arena/ and run the kernel arena tests against it and see whether it properly rejects invalid terms.
Coming to think of this again, I now see concrete value of an alternative frontend meant purely for speed: accelerate feedback for AI systems :thinking:

Arthur Paulino said:

Coming to think of this again, I now see concrete value of an alternative frontend meant purely for speed: accelerate feedback for AI systems :thinking:

It is kind of what @Kenneth Mendoza was trying to say ( I think ?).

In theory that seems correct, though in my experience the bottleneck isn't the speed of the feedback, more so the intelligence and need for trial and error. Agents can iterate for hours though, so perhaps when extending that period, the time benefit of every such call will add up to something meaningful.
I have tried to rewrite kernel in rust, but stopped #general > lean5 - rewrite everything on rust instead of c++? @ 💬

The other angle is to increase how finely incrementalised the elaborator is, which is what my undergrad thesis is partially about. This is perfectly doable while staying entirely in Lean, in fact, the code for my thesis is written in Lean. That would provide the desired "snappiness" for agentic coding.

Currently the granularity of Lean is file-level + snapshot prefixes.

maybe possible to implement https://github.com/AU-COBRA/coq-rust-extraction/ for lean

P.S. one guy already tried to rewrite in rust everything use AI, result is awful https://github.com/cool-japan/oxilean/
